content.text:
The percentile numbers were off by one because `percentile` treated a truncated rank as a 0-based index.

For sorted values `1..10`, p50 used index `5` (value `6`) instead of the 5th item (`5`). At p=100 the same formula asked for index `n`, which is past the end of the list.

It now uses nearest-rank: `ceil(p/100 * n)`, then convert to 0-based, with p=0 clamped to the minimum. p50 of `1..10` is `5`, and p=0 / p=100 return min / max. Existing tests pass.
